properties.description: Carbon-doped nickel(II) oxide with 3-coordinated Ni atoms

nodes.name: Anodization of Ni foam
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF (bulk density of 350 g m^-2, Hefei Kejing Materials Technology Co. Ltd, China) was anodized in a two-electrode system using a piece of Ni foil as the counter electrode in 0.3 M oxalic acid (Thermo Fisher Scientific, product no. 171514) solution. The anodization was carried out at the temperature of -5 °C at a constant voltage of 50 V for 10 min.

nodes.name: Rinsing, drying, and annealing
nodes.procedure: The anodized NF (nickel oxalate/NF) was then rinsed thoroughly with DI water and ethanol, successively. The anodized samples were then dried in vacuum at 100 °C for 1 h, and subsequently annealed in Ar atmosphere (ultrahigh purity 99.998%) at 400 °C for 40 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show C-doped NiO nanorod structure on NF with porous morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: b–d SEM images of the C-doped NiO nanorod/NF in different magnifications.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanoparticles with core-shell structure composed of small nanoparticle subunits in the nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images revealed that the rods are composed with small nanoparticle subunits (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringe spacings consistent with (111) and (200) crystal planes of NiO at the nanoparticle edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High resolution-TEM (HR-TEM) image collected from the edge of the nanoparticle showed lattice fringe spacings consistent with the d-spacings reported for (111) and (200) crystal planes of NiO (Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-TEM with EELS elemental mapping confirms Ni core/NiO shell structure with carbon distributed over the entire nanoparticle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field (HAADF)-TEM image of a Ni core/NiO shell particle and the corresponding EELS elemental mapping of Ni, O, and C.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS elemental mapping and line scan confirm co-presence of Ni, O, and C throughout the nanoparticle with intense O signal at the edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) elemental mapping (Fig. 2h) and line scan (inset of Fig. 2h) were collected from a representative nanoparticle, which also confirms the copresence of Ni and O in the nanoparticle.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 854.5 eV (Ni²⁺ in NiO), 855.7 eV (Ni-O-C=O), 857.1 eV (Ni³⁺); O 1s at 529.4 eV (O-Ni²⁺), 530.9 eV (O-Ni vacancy); C 1s at 288.6 eV (O-C=O); atomic concentrations Ni 53.95%, O 44.22%, C 1.83%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p peak at 854.5 eV is consistent with the value reported for Ni²⁺ in NiO... The atomic concentrations of Ni, O, and C (288.6 eV) were calculated to be 53.95%, 44.22% and 1.83%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge shows pre-peak at 529.8 eV (Ni deficient NiO), reduced 537.5 eV peak (Ni vacancies), 532.7-535 eV peaks (Ni³⁺, π*_C=O); C K-edge enhanced 288.6/290.3 eV peaks (O-C=O π*/σ*).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O K-edge XANES of the annealed NiC₂O₄·2H₂O shows a prominent pre-peak at about 529.8 eV that corresponds to... these peaks are attributed to the transition of C 1s to π* and σ* state in O-C=O.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern consistent with NiO composition; core identified as metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which is also in consistency with the NiO composition in X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Supplementary Fig. 2b... According to the XRD result, the core of the particle is metallic Ni.
